clue.text: Fat, rich USA sadly without love for another country

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters stand around the zero
sadly suggests the words are upset and knocked out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A sneer at a wealthy, overweight America lacking affection for some other nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges FAT, RICH and USA; 'without' here means outside, so those letters wrap round O (love, a zero score in tennis).
explanation.definitionFit: The republic at the southern tip of Africa is a nation distinct from the USA, hence another one.

clue.text: Load borne by you and me

parts.note: something borne by a person is on them
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A burden carried jointly by the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A responsibility or duty is a burden one carries, a figurative weight.

clue.text: Jaunt producing endless rubbish

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: tripe is slang for nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: An outing that turns up a never-ending stream of litter.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPE (rubbish, nonsense) loses its last letter, as 'endless' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A short excursion or outing for pleasure is a jaunt.

clue.text: New role man's given as hospital worker

indicators.note: New tells us the words take a fresh form, their letters rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is no letter, leaving the word man

explanation.surface: A man has a fresh job title as a hospital employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges ROLE and MAN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital social worker, historically one who handled patients' welfare, was given this title in Britain.

clue.text: Tedious course hard for woman

parts.note: a rut is a dull, unvarying routine
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dull routine proves difficult for a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in the biblical book, so a female person.

clue.text: Clown gets cask knocked over — a container of milk

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue tips the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask

explanation.surface: A circus clown topples a barrel and spills a milk churn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns TUN (a cask) round to NUT after COCO, the name of a famous circus clown.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical palm fruit holds a sweet liquid called its milk, so it is a natural vessel for it.

clue.text: Absolute dieting — a tum rumbling?

indicators.note: a rumbling tummy is churning, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a growling stomach the ultimate sign of a strict diet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumbling' rearranges DIETING, A and TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Total, out-and-out or unqualified, as in an utter disaster.

clue.text: Document rep brought out is official report

indicators.note: brought out suggests the letters are drawn out and reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sales rep produces a document that is a formal report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought out' rearranges DOCUMENT and REP into the French phrase used in English for a formal account of proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term borrowed into English for a formal written account of proceedings or a review.

clue.text: Open party a Parisian goes to

indicators.note: goes to means the first piece is placed before the party word

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is off to a celebration, as an invitation says.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or unwrap something is to open it.

clue.text: Look at the medals in this study?

definitions.text: Look at the medals in this study?

parts.words: Look at the medals in this study?
parts.note: a field of study where one examines medals, along with coins and tokens

explanation.surface: An invitation to examine military decorations as part of an academic subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The academic discipline that studies coins includes medals too.
explanation.definitionFit: The scholarly study and collecting of coins, medals and paper money.

clue.text: Fault with 's' not to the fore?

definitions.text: Fault with 's' not to the fore?

parts.words: Fault with 's' not to the fore?
parts.note: a speech defect in which the hissing sound is not produced at the front of the mouth, coming out as 'th'

explanation.surface: Asking whether some flaw involves a letter s placed out of position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to the fore' looks like a letter shuffled from the start; it means the s sound is not formed properly at the front of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment in which sibilants are pronounced with the tongue against the teeth.

clue.text: Our planet — travelling in space like a bulldozer!

parts.note: the third planet from the sun, home to us all
travelling through space is moving

explanation.surface: Our world hurtling through the cosmos like a massive bulldozer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy plant that shifts soil, such as a bulldozer, is described as this kind of equipment.

clue.text: Rod making suggestion to men in the street?

definitions.text: Rod making suggestion to men in the street?

parts.words: Rod making suggestion to men in the street?
parts.note: a striped post outside a shop hints to male passers-by that a haircut or shave awaits inside

explanation.surface: A stick that proposes something to ordinary passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men in the street' sounds like ordinary people, but it is literal: men walking past the shop are invited in for a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-and-white striped pole outside a men's hairdresser advertises the trade.

clue.text: A hit making one embarrassed

parts.note: bashed means struck hard, hit

explanation.surface: A blow that leaves someone red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ashamed or disconcerted, as when shown up in public.

clue.text: Knock the wind out of artist?

definitions.meaning: to remove gas from, to ..., as with flatulence or a fizzy drink
Edgar, the French Impressionist painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: Winding a painter, as if in a brawl at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense split as DE-GAS: take the gas, the wind, out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing gas from something is degassing, and the French painter Edgar was famous for ballet scenes.

clue.text: Drug is one of five in the east

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A medicine is one of five found in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter alkaloid from cinchona bark used as a medicine against malaria.

clue.text: Quite set free and at rest

indicators.note: set free suggests the letters are released and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Fairly liberated and relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' rearranges QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, calm and making no noise, as when resting.

clue.text: Refute objection by engineers

indicators.note: by means the two pieces sit beside each other

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Engineers raise an objection to disprove a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or disprove an argument or charge is to rebut it.

clue.text: Bishop taken in by jest is a mug

indicators.note: taken in by means the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: to toy is to trifle or jest with something
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman is fooled by a prank, making him a sucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a dupe; it is a drinking jug shaped like a seated man, called a Toby jug in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a drinking vessel moulded as a stout man in a tricorn hat.

clue.text: Bundle of mischief

definitions.meaning: a large tied bundle of hay, cotton or straw
an archaic word for evil, harm or woe, as in baleful

explanation.surface: A child described as a little troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied pack of hay is called this, and an old word meaning harm survives in baleful.

clue.text: Animal arrived, then left

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: A creature turned up and then departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A humped desert mammal, a beast of burden.

clue.text: Person making demand but not one calling out

indicators.note: but not tells us the following item is removed from the word

parts.note: a claimant makes a claim or demand
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A person demanding something who stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAIMANT loses I (one, as a Roman numeral), as 'but not' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for noisy or insistent, clamouring for attention.

clue.text: Maiden in hollow with nothing on engenders ridicule

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the word for the hollow

parts.note: a lap can be a hollow among hills
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl in a dip wearing nothing provokes mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M (maiden, from cricket scoring) inside LAP, a hollow; 'with' adds O (nothing) and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise or mock someone publicly is to ridicule them.

clue.text: People start to talk in lessons

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for lessons

parts.note: morals are the lessons drawn from a story

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Humans begin to chat during class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives T from talk, and 'in' puts it inside MORALS, the lessons of a fable.
explanation.definitionFit: Human beings, as opposed to gods, are those who must die.

clue.text: The final bit constructed from lead and tin

indicators.note: constructed from says a new thing is built out of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A last piece made from two metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed from' rearranges LEAD and TIN; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The very last part of something, such as the closing batsmen in cricket, is its tail.

clue.text: Nobs sending flashy fellow back

indicators.note: sending back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a spiv is a flashily dressed petty crook, British slang

explanation.surface: Toffs dismiss a show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending back' turns SPIV, a flashily dressed wheeler-dealer in British slang, round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobs are posh, important people, and these initials stand for very important persons.

clue.text: The man on record for being an abject toady

parts.note: he is the man
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: The man appears on a disc as a grovelling flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is Dickens's byword for an obsequious, ever so humble crawler.

clue.text: Priest gets wicked learner dragged to the front

indicators.note: dragged to the front means the letter is pulled from its place to the start

parts.note: evil means wicked
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A clergyman with an evil novice hauled forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In EVIL (wicked) the L (learner) is moved to the front by 'dragged to the front'; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the tribe of Levi supplied the priests, and Levi is its founder.

clue.text: Salmon provided by Henry's wife

definitions.meaning: a young salmon in its early freshwater stage
Catherine, the sixth and last wife of King Henry VIII

explanation.surface: Fish supplied by the king's queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A young river salmon carries this name, as did Catherine, Henry VIII's surviving sixth queen.

clue.text: Am OK, the paye having been dealt with — this is left!

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters are handled and dealt out like cards in a new order

parts.note: PAYE, pay as you earn, is the British income tax deducted at source

explanation.surface: Relief that the tax deduction is sorted, and here is what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been dealt with' rearranges AM, OK, THE and PAYE; PAYE is British pay-as-you-earn tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Net earnings are what remains of wages once tax and deductions are removed.

clue.text: Coming from garden, I leave flowing water

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener says goodbye to the stream running past.
explanation.definitionFit: The great African river is a body of moving water.

clue.text: Account by writer — it's first brought back for magistrate maybe

indicators.note: brought back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the three letters
a pen is a writing instrument
a diary is a daily account of events

explanation.surface: A writer's journal describes a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN (writer) by DIARY (account), with 'first' putting ITS, turned round by 'brought back', at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaried magistrate in Britain, paid unlike lay justices.
